name: The Meridian Unsolved Archive
creator: Yusra Halvorsen-Ndiaye
description: A meticulously researched true crime podcast investigating cold cases, disappearances, and unexplained deaths from across GLMZ's full tier range, with particular attention to cases that received inadequate official investigation due to the victim's tier status. Host Yusra Halvorsen-Ndiaye is a former Axiom Municipal Authority records clerk who uses her institutional knowledge to navigate the city's labyrinthine documentation systems. The show's production quality is high but deliberately unglamorous — no music stings, no dramatic pauses, just careful narration and source audio where available.
cultural_impact: The show's 2207 season on the 'Ward 4 Disappearances' — seventeen Shelf residents who vanished within eight months with no official investigation opened — prompted a citizen pressure campaign that eventually forced a partial municipal inquiry.
controversy: Halvorsen-Ndiaye was served with a data suppression order in 2210 by a Tier 4 private security corponation whose contractors appeared in her investigation of a Tier 2 labor dispute death; she read the suppression order aloud on the following episode.
story_hooks: Halvorsen-Ndiaye's research into a decade-old Shelf disappearance leads her to a still-living person who very much does not want to be found — and who may have disappeared deliberately.
A former Axiom Municipal Authority officer begins feeding Yusra classified case files anonymously; the information is genuine but the motivation is unclear and possibly dangerous.
The show receives a neural-feed message from someone claiming to be a victim featured in an earlier episode — a victim Halvorsen-Ndiaye reported as deceased.
